profile.headline: LLM, RAG, VLM and AI agent research and systems, M.S. student in Computer Engineering
profile.summaryLead: I'm interested in getting AI to give answers you can trust, not just answers that sound plausible.
summary: I have researched video question answering that holds back when evidence is thin, and RAG that shifts its retrieval weights by question type. I have also built answers that rewrite only what changed when sensor values shift, and an AI agent that moves equipment only after a person approves; all of it comes from the same interest.

I used to enjoy wiring things up from device firmware to web pages and watching features actually work. Connecting a public AI model to a service during my Kakao internship drew me into this field, and writing papers gave me the habit of checking what improved and why with experiments under the same conditions.

These days I build with coding agents such as pi, dsh, Claude Code and Codex, and in Cursor I try out several coding LLM APIs connected through a proxy. I also enjoy making tools for agents, like having them cross-review each other's results or plugging in Notion as their memory. I designed a way to split a GPU server shared by several labs into per-user workspaces, and every lab now uses the server that way.

rag.title: Question-adaptive Retrieval and Grounded Answers
rag.desc: I combine keyword, vector and graph retrieval with weights fixed per question type, removing the extra LLM call per question, and connect retrieved documents to answers as evidence. In SmartFarm RAG this raised nDCG@10 from 0.72 to 0.90 over an equal-proportion mix, published as a first-author KCI paper; in on-device medical question answering it raised RAGAS answer relevancy from 0.52 to 0.69 on the PC development path. I also applied the three-retriever structure to aerospace document question answering.
rag.body:
I combine keyword, vector and graph retrieval with weights fixed per question type, removing the extra LLM call per question, and connect retrieved documents to answers as evidence. In SmartFarm RAG this raised nDCG@10 from 0.72 to 0.90 over an equal-proportion mix, published as a first-author KCI paper; in on-device medical question answering it raised RAGAS answer relevancy from 0.52 to 0.69 on the PC development path. I also applied the three-retriever structure to aerospace document question answering.

## Choosing what a question needs

Built a safe-retrieval fallback for weak graph evidence or failed configuration checks, and a flow that shows the documents used in each answer.

## What I want to explore next

Refining chunking and indexing rules for domain document structure, and evaluating retrieval relevance and answer grounding together to raise accuracy and speed on edge and on-device setups.

sensor-operations.title: Answer Revision on Sensor Change and Approval-based Operations
sensor-operations.desc: I research operations support that links answer sentences to the sensor values they depend on, rewrites only the affected answer units when values change, and controls equipment only after operator approval.
sensor-operations.body:
I research operations support that links answer sentences to the sensor values they depend on, rewrites only the affected answer units when values change, and controls equipment only after operator approval.

## Operations that reflect the current state

In my master's thesis research, re-checking sensor state just before execution and revising only the affected answer units kept the same response-state consistency as full regeneration while rewriting 26.5% less. In the SmartFarm operations-support system I check the quality and change of observed values and execute only operator-approved adjustments through to a result check. Validation is limited to a simulator and does not represent real farm-control performance.

## What I want to explore next

Lowering the cost of updating dependencies when sensor values change continuously, and showing the evidence behind judgements and the action history in a way users can follow.

## Related project

[Implementation and my role](/projects/llm-selective-revision)

smartfarm-rag.name: Query-adaptive Retrieval and SmartFarm Operations Support
smartfarm-rag.desc: Combined keyword, vector and graph retrieval with weights fixed per question type, removing the extra LLM call per question, and built an MCP server for AI agents that executes control only after operator approval.
smartfarm-rag.metric: nDCG@10 0.72→0.90, about 12% faster edge responses, KCI first-author paper
smartfarm-rag.body:
Combined keyword, vector and graph retrieval with weights fixed per question type, removing the extra LLM call per question, and built an MCP server for AI agents that executes control only after operator approval.

## My role

Designed the research method, implemented retrieval and the MCP server, compared it with existing approaches, and wrote the first-author paper.

## What I built

Combined keyword, vector and graph retrieval with weights fixed per question type, removing the extra LLM call per question. When graph evidence is weak or configuration validation fails, retrieval falls back to a safe mode.

The MCP server for AI agents separates read and control tools, executes control only after operator approval, and logs every request.

## Comparison and operations validation

Evidence: nDCG@10 0.72→0.90, about 12% faster edge responses, KCI first-author paper

Compared with combining the three retrievers in equal proportion, nDCG@10 rose from 0.72 to 0.90, and edge-device response time fell by about 12% compared with choosing weights with an LLM for every question. The operations-support system connects observations, document evidence, AI explanations, operator approval and execution-result checks; this operational flow was validated in simulation.

## Technologies

Python, RAG, MCP, FastAPI, Docker, GitHub Actions

mv-evirag.name: Selective Response for Multi-View Video Question Answering
mv-evirag.desc: Separated view selection, answerability and answer release for multi-view CCTV video into stages, and fine-tuned a VLM with LoRA to answer when evidence is present and abstain when it is not.
mv-evirag.metric: Wrong answers 27→0 and correct answers 140→247 over the same model given only an abstention instruction; first-author international journal paper under review
mv-evirag.body:
Separated view selection, answerability and answer release for multi-view CCTV video into stages, and fine-tuned a VLM with LoRA to answer when evidence is present and abstain when it is not.

## My role

Led research design, model training and implementation, comparative experiments, and first-author writing.

## View selection and response decisions

A relevant person may appear in a video while the part needed to judge an action is occluded. Input selection and answerability were therefore handled as separate decisions, with the information available at each stage kept apart.

Training on both evidence-bearing and evidence-deficient inputs taught the model to answer when the video holds evidence and abstain when it does not. After generating an answer, response confidence decides whether to release it.

## Evaluation and publication

Evidence: Wrong answers 27→0 and correct answers 140→247 over the same model given only an abstention instruction; first-author international journal paper under review

Evaluation items and comparison conditions were fixed before the experiments, and answer coverage was evaluated together with errors. The same model given only an abstention instruction also abstained on answerable questions, while the fine-tuned model cut wrong answers from 27 to 0 and raised correct answers from 140 to 247.

Paper: Role-Separated Selective Response for Question Answering in Multi-View Video Surveillance (under review at IEEE Access, submitted August 2026, first author)

## Technologies

Implemented training and evaluation code in Python and PyTorch and fine-tuned the VLM with LoRA. Video evaluation used inputs with regions of interest and rule-defined information-availability conditions.

cross-review-bridge.name: Codex Plugin for Approval-gated External AI Review
cross-review-bridge.desc: A harness tool for Codex Desktop: when an external AI such as ChatGPT web reviews the work, a person approves what is sent, and the returned feedback is verified locally before it is applied.
cross-review-bridge.metric: Implemented a cross-review loop with review briefs, secret redaction, human approval, and feedback triage
cross-review-bridge.body:
A harness tool for Codex Desktop: when an external AI such as ChatGPT web reviews the work, a person approves what is sent, and the returned feedback is verified locally before it is applied.

## Overview

Coding agents work fast inside a local workspace, but a second opinion from a stronger reviewer catches design and correctness issues. Sending project content to an external service needs a human decision and a local check of what comes back, so this is turned into a repeatable, approval-gated loop.

## Implementation

- Builds review briefs from local project context, and ZIP packages that carry the full working context.
- Redacts common secret patterns before generating a brief.
- Asks for human approval before sending project content to an external AI.
- Triages returned feedback as apply, consider, reject or needs a user decision, and verifies it locally before applying it.

## Technologies

Codex plugin and skills, PowerShell

llm-selective-revision.name: Selective Revision of LLM Answers on Sensor Change
llm-selective-revision.desc: Researched and implemented a method that links answer sentences to the sensor values they depend on and rewrites only the affected answer units when those values change.
llm-selective-revision.metric: Rewrites 26.5% less while keeping the same response-state consistency as full regeneration
llm-selective-revision.body:
Researched and implemented a method that links answer sentences to the sensor values they depend on and rewrites only the affected answer units when those values change.

## My role

Research design, implementation of the selective-revision structure, comparison with full regeneration, and writing the master's thesis.

## What I built

Each answer sentence is linked to the sensor values it depends on, and when a value changes only the affected answer units are rewritten. Sensor state is checked again just before the answer is used for an action, so the answer does not drift from the current state.

## Results

Evidence: Rewrites 26.5% less while keeping the same response-state consistency as full regeneration

Compared with regenerating the whole answer whenever a sensor value changes, it keeps the same response-state consistency while rewriting 26.5% less.

## Technologies

Python, pytest, GitHub Actions
